# 2 Baruch Chapter 9 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 9:1 — "plantation of your right hand"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-plantation-of-your-right-hand" | Literal construct chain |
| LOGOS | "the plantation of your right hand" | Formal, preserves Ps 80:15 allusion |
| PNEUMA | "the garden you planted with your own hand" | Paraphrases the idiom; more vivid |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. The phrase echoes Ps 80:15 ("the vine...that your right hand has planted"). Preserving "plantation of your right hand" maintains the intertextual connection. PNEUMA's expansion loses the compactness of the allusion.

---

## 9:2 — "no one left here to comfort your servant Baruch"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "there-is-no-one-left [here] to-comfort your-servant Baruch" | Literal with implied "here" bracketed |
| LOGOS | "there is no one left here to comfort your servant Baruch" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "There is no one left here to comfort me, your servant" | First-person shift; "me" for "Baruch" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. Third-person self-reference "your servant Baruch" is a standard Syriac lament form (cf. "your servant David"). PNEUMA's first-person shift loses the formal petition register.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 2**
